text:
anna_support: FYI — ACME reported their Dedicated capacity dashboard lost node/GPU rows right after they applied a cluster kubelet + CNI upgrade. They opened a high-priority support case.

mike_sre: Can you paste the customer cluster ID and a quick repro?

anna_support: cluster: acme-prod-01, they upgraded to kubelet 1.28.2 and CNI calico v3.24 -> v3.27 yesterday evening. Dashboard panel shows total GPUs 0 for two nodepools that definitely have GPUs. Customer sent this snippet from their UI: `No matching nodes for pool gpu-west-1a`.

julia_platform: Noted. Did they see any kubelet/node renames or node IDs change? That usually breaks our inventory mapping.

anna_support: They said node names are unchanged but their metrics agent logs show TLS handshake failures to our telemetry endpoint around the upgrade window. They attached daemonset logs. Key excerpt:```stderr
2026-03-16T22:12:04Z telemetry-agent error: handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority```

kevin_oncall: That would cause the agent to stop shipping node/GPU metrics, which would drop rows. Any pod restarts on telemetry-agent?

anna_support: Yes — daemonset restarted repeatedly. Here's the crash loop count from customer: `kubectl -n infra get pods | grep telemetry-agent` -> `telemetry-agent-abcde CrashLoopBackOff 5/15`

mike_sre: Ok, two hypotheses: 1) telemetry-agent lost trust of control-plane after CNI change and stopped pushing metrics; 2) node identity mismatch (nodeName vs reported hostname) after kubelet flags changed, so our inventory join failed. Which one matches logs?

anna_support: Logs show both TLS errors and entries like `reported_node_name=ip-10-4-2-17.ec2.internal, kube_node_name=ip-10-4-2-17`. But around rollouts some lines show `reported_node_name=ip-10-4-2-17.localdomain` — small suffix change.

julia_platform: That suffix change will break our node-name normalization in inventory sync. Our join key is node.metadata.name sanitized by dns. If telemetry reports a different hostname, GPU metrics don't attach to node rows.

mike_sre: Short-term mitigation: restart telemetry daemonset on affected clusters to re-establish TLS and push current metrics, and run the inventory-sync job with a relaxed normalization rule. I'll outline commands.

mike_sre: Commands:```bash
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/telemetry-agent
kubectl -n infra logs -l app=telemetry-agent --tail=200
# run inventory sync job (platform team)
kubectl -n redwood-platform create job --from=cronjob/inventory-sync temp-inventory-sync-1976
```

anna_support: I ran the rollout restart with the customer (with their APM) and the agent came back healthy on 6/8 nodes. They reported GPU rows started to reappear in ~2m but two nodes still missing.

kevin_oncall: For remaining two nodes, we should check if the agent is reporting same node identifier as k8s. Ask customer for `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl -n infra logs telemetry-agent-<pod>` for those nodes.

anna_support: Sent request, they returned `kubectl get nodes -o wide` — both nodes show `INTERNAL-DNS: ip-10-4-2-21.localdomain`. telemetry-agent log shows `X509 error` for one node and for the other it shows `hostname mismatch: expected ip-10-4-2-21.ec2.internal`.

mike_sre: So one node still failing TLS — certs likely rotated during upgrade and agent trust store wasn't refreshed. The hostname mismatch is the normalization issue. I'll push a quick platform-side workaround: accept either suffix in inventory join and trigger an on-demand full inventory reindex.

julia_platform: I'll kick the reindex job now and add tolerant normalization rules to the inventory-sync config (safe for 24h window). After reindex we should see the two missing GPU rows return.

deploy-bot: job/inventory-reindex-1976543210 started by julia_platform (pod: reindex-xyz).

kevin_oncall: Customer notified. They are watching dashboards. Keep me posted if anything else flakes.

anna_support: Update from ACME: after reindex + restart, dashboard shows all GPU rows back, metrics stable. They still want root cause.

mike_sre: Root cause summary to include in the case: concurrent kubelet/CNI upgrade caused 1) TLS cert rotation issues for telemetry-agent on a subset of nodes, causing metric ingestion gaps and 2) node hostname suffix change for a small number of nodes that broke our strict normalization logic. Both contributed to missing node/GPU rows.

julia_platform: Action items: 1) make inventory-sync hostname matching tolerant to common suffixes (PR open), 2) add telemetry-agent health alert on metric TLS errors, 3) add post-upgrade checklist to support runbook (restart telemetry + reindex if metrics gaps).

anna_support: Customer happy with patch and runbook. Closing case after follow-up doc. :white_check_mark:
